captions.detailed: This 3D model consists of two identical 90-degree curved rod segments, or quarter-rings, arranged symmetrically on a flat plane. Each segment has a circular cross-section, giving it a smooth, tubular appearance. One end of each segment features a small cylindrical projection (a connector nib), while the opposite end has a matching cylindrical indentation (an anti-nib socket) to allow interlocking connection.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric OpenSCAD script that generates two quarter-circle segments of a ring with connector nibs at the ends. The user should be able to adjust parameters such as the wheel radius, tube thickness, and toggles for adding sacrificial print support under the connector nibs.
captions.factory: The design is built around a custom module 'wheelquarter' that creates a 90-degree segment of a torus. This is achieved by taking a full torus (created via rotate_extrude of a circle) and using difference with two large cubes to cut away three-quarters of the circle. A cylindrical pocket (anti-nib) is subtracted from one end, while a cylinder (nib) is added to the other end. Sacrificial support is optionally generated underneath the nib using a small thin cube.
